Single pass while remembering the cheapest price seen so far. Each day, the best sale today is price − minSoFar; keep the maximum of that.

1. minPrice = p[0], best = 0.
  2. For each later day: best = max(best, p[i] − minPrice).
  3. Then minPrice = min(minPrice, p[i]).
  4. Print best.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every buy day i and every later sell day j and keep the best difference.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Track the minimum price so far; selling today earns price − min, so one pass finds the best.

explain: For 7 1 5 3 6 4: the minimum becomes 1 on day 1; selling at 5 earns 4, at 3 earns 2, at 6 earns 5 (the best), at 4 earns 3, so the answer is 5. Updating the profit before the minimum makes sure we never buy and sell on the same day after the future. If prices only fall, every difference is ≤ 0, so best stays 0. A single day also gives 0.
recognize: "Buy once, sell later, maximise profit" → running minimum and best difference in one pass.
python:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
p = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
lo, best = p[0], 0
for x in p[1:]:
    best = max(best, x - lo)
    lo = min(lo, x)
print(best)
